title: Delivery Of Letter Addressed To Mr. D. Milne - Australian Trade Commissioner Informed

page_data.en:
FORM NO. 3
G. ROM-14-36

CONFIDENTIAL

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No............

Section 1, Special Branch Shanghai,
REPORT
Date October 19, 1937.

Subject (in full) Delivery of letter addressed to Mr. D. Milne - Australian
Trade Commissioner informed.

Made by D.S. Lockwood    Forwarded by 〔此处转录不清〕

On the morning of October 19, 1937, Mr. V. G. Bowden,
Australian Trade Commissioner in China, was informed that
the letter addressed to Mr. D. Milne had been delivered to
a Mr. S. L. Ling at the Central Bank of China. He was also
informed that Mr. Ling would acknowledge receipt of the
letter if he cared to ring up telephone number 74580 or
70001.

In reply, Mr. Bowden stated that he had received
information that Mr. D. Milne was now in Canton. He wished
to express his thanks for the action taken by the Police
in locating the whereabouts of Mr. D. Milne.

J. A. Lockwood
ap.    J. S.
〔此处转录不清〕
D. C. (Special Branch)
〔此处转录不清〕

第一节，上海特别处，
报告
日期：1937年10月19日。

事由（全称）：告知澳大利亚贸易专员关于寄给 D. Milne 先生信件的递送情况。

制作人：D.S. Lockwood    转呈人：〔此处转录不清〕

1937年10月19日上午，驻华澳大利亚贸易专员 V. G. Bowden 先生获悉，寄给 D. Milne 先生的信件已送达中国银行的一位 S. L. Ling 先生手中。他还被告知，如果 Ling 先生愿意，可致电 74580 或 70001 确认收悉该信件。

作为回复，Bowden 先生表示，他已收到消息，D. Milne 先生目前在广州。他对警方为查明 D. Milne 先生下落所采取的行动表示感谢。

J. A. Lockwood
ap.    J. S.
〔此处转录不清〕
D. C. (特别处)
〔此处转录不清〕

FORM NO. 3
G. 20M-11-36

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No.__________
（印：CONFIDENTIAL REPORT） S.2 Special Branch Section,
Date October 16 1937.

Subject (in full) Delivery of letter addressed to Mr. D. Milne.

Made by__________ and __________ Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

The letter, addressed to Mr. D. Milne by
Mr. Bowden, was delivered by a special messenger to
Mr. S.L. Ling at the Central Bank of China this morning.
Mr. Ling telephoned stating he is unable to issue a written
acknowledgment as it will mean leakage of military secrets.
He will however give a verbal acknowledgment if Mr. Bowden
will ring him up (Tel No. 74580 or 70001).

Tan Shaoliang
Superintendent.

D. C. (Special Branch)
S/
Jaspon M Bowden

（批：MB）
OCT 1937

CONFIDENTIAL

G. 4 M 1-36
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No. ____
S.2 Special Branch XXXX
REPORT
Date. October 15 1937.

Subject ............ Disappearance of Mr. D. Milne.

Made by ............ and ............ Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

Enquiries have been made at the Passport Office,
Woosung-Shanghai Martial Law Headquarters and the Shanghai
Office of the Waichiaopu. They have no record of any person
bearing this name (D. Milne) having obtained a visa for
Nanking or a Military Pass for the trip.
Not satisfied with the above information, I continued
enquiries at the Park Hotel. The Chinese Manager, Mr. Lu,
informed me confidentially that during his stay in the hotel
between August 29 and September 1, Mr. Milne was visited
frequently by a Cantonese named Lu Bing Cham, that both went
to Nanking at the same time and that all bills for hotel
charges, etc. were paid by Mr. S.L. Ling 林世良, Departmental Chief
of the Central Bank of China, a close follower of Dr. H.H.Kung.
Mr. Ling being an acquaintance of mine, was approached for
information. He states that D. Milne went to Nanking on Sept. 1
where he has succeeded in obtaining orders for a large consignment
of supplies (? war supplies) from Australia. He returned to
Shanghai once about a fortnight ago but is now believed to be at
Nanking again. Prior to leaving Shanghai on September 1, he is
said to have called on the British Consulate-General for advice.
Mr. Ling refuses to reveal the address of Mr. D.Milne
at Nanking, but states he is quite safe and Mr. Ling will
undertake to deliver all letters addressed to Mr. Milne, c/o Mr. Ling
the Central Bank of China, Shanghai.

Superintendent.
D. C. (Special Branch)

上海公共租界工部局警务处。    档案号. ____
S.2 特别处 XXXX
报告
日期：1937年10月15日。

事由  ____  D. Milne 先生失踪案。

制作人：  ____  和  ____  转呈人：督察长 Tan Shao Liang

已在护照办公室、吴淞-上海戒严司令部以及外交部上海办事处进行了查询。他们没有任何记录显示有此姓名（D. Milne）的人获得过前往南京的签证或旅行军用通行证。
对上述信息不满意，我继续在派克饭店（Park Hotel）进行调查。中方经理 Lu 先生私下告诉我，Milne 先生在8月29日至9月1日入住酒店期间，经常有一位名叫 Lu Bing Cham 的广东人来访，两人同时前往南京，且所有酒店账单等费用均由中国银行部门主管、孔祥熙博士的亲信林世良（S.L. Ling）先生支付。Ling 先生是我的熟人，我便向他探询信息。他表示，D. Milne 于9月1日前往南京，在那里成功获得了来自澳大利亚的大宗物资（？军需品）订单。他大约两周前曾返回上海一次，但据信现在又回到了南京。据说在9月1日离开上海之前，他曾拜访英国总领事馆寻求建议。
Ling 先生拒绝透露 D. Milne 先生在南京的地址，但表示他很安全，并且 Ling 先生承诺将转交所有寄给 Milne 先生、由上海中国银行 Ling 先生代收的信件。

督察长。
D. C. (特别处)

TELEGRAPHIC ADDRESS
"AUSTRADE"

TELEPHONES 17202
           17203

REFERENCE No.

COMMONWEALTH OF AUSTRALIA

OFFICE OF THE
AUSTRALIAN TRADE COMMISSIONER
IN CHINA

12 THE BUND
SHANGHAI. 12th October, 1937.

PLEASE ADDRESS REPLY TO:
P. O. Box 1580
SHANGHAI

The Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
185 Foochow Road,
LOCAL.

Dear Sir,

On the night 31st August last I received a telephone call from a man who described himself as an Australian commercial traveller named D. Milne, and who told me that he was intending to leave the following day by road for Nanking in the hope of being able to secure orders from the National Government for supplies of provisions, uniform cloth, etc., from Australia. He gave me no indication as to when he expected to come back to Shanghai, but as my Government has asked me to interest myself in the safety of Australians here I enquired of the Park Hotel on 5th instant as to whether he had returned. They replied that he had left on 1st September for Nanking, leaving no forwarding address, and that they had had no subsequent news of him. I also had enquiries made of the Cathay, Metropole and Palace Hotels and at Cathay Mansions and Medhurst, and was told that he had not registered at any of these.

I then wrote (on 5th inst.) to the British Consulate-General here asking if they had any knowledge of his movements and was informed verbally that they had no record of him here but had wired to the Consulate in Nanking enquiring regarding him. Yesterday Mr. A.G.N. Ogden telephoned me that a reply had been received from the Consulate in Nanking to the effect that they could find no trace of him there.

电报挂号

电话 17202
           17203

驻华
澳大利亚贸易专员办事处

上海外滩12号。1937年10月12日。

回信请寄：
上海邮政信箱 1580

警务总监，
上海公共租界工部局，
福州路185号，
本市。

亲爱的先生：

去年8月31日晚，我接到一个自称是澳大利亚商业推销员、名为 D. Milne 的男子的电话，他告诉我，他打算第二天陆路前往南京，希望能从国民政府那里获得澳大利亚供应的食品、制服布料等的订单。他没有向我表明预计何时返回上海，但由于我国政府要求我关注在此地澳大利亚人的安全，我于本月5日向派克饭店查询他是否已返回。他们回答说，他已于9月1日前往南京，未留转寄地址，此后也没有他的消息。我还让人在华懋公寓（Cathay）、大都会饭店（Metropole）、华懋饭店（Palace Hotels）以及华懋公寓大楼（Cathay Mansions）和麦特赫司脱公寓（Medhurst）进行了查询，得知他并未在这些地方登记。

随后，我于本月5日致函此地英国总领事馆，询问他们是否知晓其行踪，并获口头答复称，他们这里没有他的记录，但已致电南京领事馆查询他的情况。昨天，A.G.N. Ogden 先生致电告诉我，已收到南京领事馆的回复，称在那里找不到他的踪迹。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

I am making further enquiries in Nanking through
private (Australian) channels, as it would seem really to
be there that one must look for him, but in order to satisfy
myself that he has not returned here I should be very
grateful if you would make such enquiries as you can here
with a view to learning anything you can regarding his move-
ments.

I may say that, from his conversation with me by
telephone, it would seem that he was in touch with Chinese
here who had been advising him regarding his trip to Nanking.
I would add further that I have never met the man himself
and know nothing of him except for his telephone conversation
with me above referred to.

Thanking you in anticipation of your kind co-opera-
tion in this matter,

I am,

Yours very truly,

(V. G. Bowden)
AUSTRALIAN TRADE COMMISSIONER IN CHINA.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

我正通过私人（澳大利亚）渠道在南京作进一步查询，因为看来确实应该去那里寻找他，但为了让我自己确信他并未返回此地，如蒙贵处尽可能在此地进行查询，以了解有关其行踪的任何情况，我将不胜感激。

我可以补充说，从他在电话中与我的谈话来看，他似乎与在此地的中国人有联系，这些人曾就他前往南京之行向他提供建议。我还要补充一点，我从未见过此人本人，除了上述提到的他与我的电话交谈外，我对他一无所知。

预先感谢您在此事上的 kindly 合作，

此致，

您最真诚的，

(V. G. Bowden)
驻华澳大利亚贸易专员。

him. Wsterday Mr. A.G.N. Ogden telephoned me that a reply 
had been received from the Consulate in Nanking to the effect 
that they could find no trace of him there. 


I am making further enquiries in Nanking through 
private (Australian) channels, as it would seem really to 
be there that one must look for him, but in order to satisfy 
myself that he has not returned here I should be very 
grateful if you would make such enquiries as you can here 
with a view to learning anything you can regarding his move- 
ments. 


I may say that, from his conversation with me by 
telephone, it would seem that he was in touch with Chinese 
here who had been advising him regarding his trip to Nanking. 
I would add further that I have never met the man himself 
and know nothing of him except for his telephone conversation 
with me above referred to.
